courses.description: Introduces data preparation, programming, statistics, learning methods, visualization and responsible AI through projects with real datasets.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): None

category_review.rationale: The broad introduction deliberately spans programming, mathematical analysis and AI methods without establishing one dominant subject.

courses.description: Develops prediction and inference workflows with regression, classification, decision trees, dimensionality reduction, feature engineering and bias-variance analysis.

category_review.rationale: After a brief mathematics review, the description explicitly centers introductory machine-learning methods and predictive data workflows.

requirements.title: Basic science
requirements.summary: Eligible prefixes: BB, CH, GE, PH. The program page omits quantity; the separately sourced university baseline requires at least 2/3 unit of natural or engineering science.

requirements.title: Six electives across three categories
requirements.summary: Six electives across three categories

requirements.title: Business Analytics Applications (Select at least 3)
requirements.summary: At least three courses in business analytics applications.

requirements.title: Computing Technologies, Data and Mathematical Sciences (Maximum 3)
requirements.summary: At most three: CS3000+ except CS3043; DS/MA2000+; CS2119 or MIS2300.

requirements.title: Business and Entrepreneurship (Maximum 2):
requirements.summary: At most two: previously unused OBC courses, BUS1020/BUS2020, ETR courses, or MIS3010.

requirements.title: Major Qualifying Project
requirements.summary: Required senior capstone supervised by full-time Business School faculty who teach analytics, AI or STEM.

requirements.title: Overlap and double-major restrictions
requirements.summary: Each course fills only one program slot. A simultaneous Marketing Analytics major is prohibited.

requirements.title: Graduate-course substitutions
requirements.summary: WPI limits on graduate credit apply. Admission to a graduate business program must precede graduate business courses; undergraduate versions do not satisfy corresponding graduate requirements.

requirements.title: Transfer after matriculation
requirements.summary: Off-campus study after WPI matriculation needs prior written permission for transferable credit.

requirements.title: Minimum academic credit
requirements.summary: Earn at least 15 academic units; use free electives beyond published distribution requirements to reach the minimum.

requirements.title: Residence
requirements.summary: At least eight units must be completed satisfactorily in residence at WPI.

requirements.title: Humanities and arts
requirements.summary: Two units with the applicable humanities/arts sequence and completion evaluation.

requirements.title: Mathematics and science baseline
requirements.summary: Two units in science, engineering, mathematics or computing, subject to the program’s stricter distribution.

requirements.title: Quantitative science baseline
requirements.summary: At least 2/3 unit in quantitative science; eligible subjects are determined by the major.

requirements.title: Natural or engineering science baseline
requirements.summary: At least 2/3 unit in natural or engineering science; the major determines eligible subjects.

requirements.title: Remaining science baseline
requirements.summary: The remaining 2/3 unit may be quantitative, natural or engineering science.

requirements.title: Interactive Qualifying Project
requirements.summary: At least one unit of an approved project relating science/technology to society, with required documentation.

requirements.title: Major Qualifying Project
requirements.summary: At least one unit of an approved project in the major, with required documentation. This includes rather than adds to the program MQP.

requirements.title: Program distribution certification
requirements.summary: Complete the major’s published distribution; certification is by its Program Review Committee on adviser recommendation.

requirements.title: Social sciences
requirements.summary: At least 2/3 social-science unit, excluding qualifying-project work.

requirements.title: Wellness and physical education
requirements.summary: Complete 1/3 WPE unit (normally four classes) or an approved equivalent.

requirements.title: Standard humanities sequence
requirements.summary: Complete five HUA courses before HU3900/HU3910 or an equivalent 1/3-unit inquiry seminar/practicum; submit the completion form afterward.

requirements.title: Thematic depth
requirements.summary: Before the capstone, take at least three related courses in AR, MU, TH, EN/WR/RH, HI/HU/INTL, PY/RE, or a faculty-approved interdisciplinary theme.

requirements.title: Depth level
requirements.summary: At least one depth course preceding the capstone must be at 2000 level or above. A 3000-level course is encouraged, not required.

requirements.title: Breadth outside depth area
requirements.summary: Before the capstone, take a course outside the depth grouping. Groups: AR/TH/MU; SP/GN/ISE/AB/CN; EN/WR/RH; HI/HU/INTL; PY/RE. Six-course modern-language sequences are exempt.

requirements.title: Language alternatives
requirements.summary: Language paths: a practicum as the sixth language course; an advanced seminar after five language courses; or advanced-placement language competence with a mixed approved sequence ending in an advanced seminar.

requirements.title: Non-native English path
requirements.summary: Non-native English speakers may combine ISE/WR work and conclude with a project-based ISE/WR course at 3000 level or above.

requirements.title: Practicum permission
requirements.summary: Instructor permission is required for the practicum.

requirements.title: Advanced placement ceiling
requirements.summary: At most 1/3 AP unit counts toward HUA. German/Spanish scores 4–5 qualify subject to the starting-course restriction; studio art requires portfolio review. Additional AP credit may satisfy other requirements.

requirements.title: Transfer completion alternatives
requirements.summary: Transfers with fewer than six HUA courses complete the remaining two-unit sequence including a capstone. Two units completed before entry may satisfy HUA through coordinator approval of the completion form.

requirements.title: Transfer-credit evaluation
requirements.summary: The general HUA rule accepts accredited US courses at B- or better; non-US work is individually reviewed. Prior approval is required after matriculation. The language subsection also retains legacy B/C thresholds and recommends B-; obtain coordinator determination for that conflict.

requirements.title: Prior language study
requirements.summary: Without AP, three years of high-school language may yield 1/3 transfer unit after two WPI courses at intermediate level or above. AP/high-school pathways require starting WPI language study at Elementary II or above.

requirements.title: Off-campus humanities alternative
requirements.summary: An approved HUA project-center term may combine with at least three prior HUA courses/equivalents. HUA admission, required forms, adviser-directed preparation, written report and any required presentation apply; normally finish within one term under HUA faculty supervision.

requirements.title: Eligible social sciences
requirements.summary: Two SSPS courses qualify: ECON, ENV, DEV, GOV, PSY, SD, SOC, SS or STS. SS/ID2050 qualifies. A 1/3-unit Great Problems Seminar may qualify only with a co-teacher holding at least a half-time SSPS appointment.

requirements.title: Social science exclusions
requirements.summary: HUA, Business School and STEM social-implications courses do not qualify; CS3043/SS3043, IMGD2000 and EDU4100 are specifically excluded.

requirements.title: Social-science overlap
requirements.summary: Eligible social-science courses may also satisfy major distribution requirements.

requirements.title: Wellness alternatives and approval
requirements.summary: Repeated WPE courses may earn credit; independent study is unavailable. Approved varsity/club participation requires advance registration (varsity instructor permission); approved off-campus courses require advance approval. No retroactive credit. Some ROTC participation qualifies after commander review.

requirements.title: IQP preparation
requirements.summary: Global Projects Program IQPs require a preparation course before travel. Projects may be on or off campus; reports are archived in Digital WPI.

requirements.title: MQP disciplinary context
requirements.summary: The MQP applies disciplinary knowledge to a representative professional problem, selected with the adviser to complement the overall program. A preliminary proposal is encouraged, not universally required.

requirements.title: Credit-bearing completion
requirements.summary: A/B/C are undergraduate course grades that earn credit; NR does not. IQP/MQP/HUA require an overall completion evaluation; project SP is temporary and must be replaced by a permanent grade.

requirements.title: No institutional undergraduate GPA
requirements.summary: WPI does not maintain an undergraduate cumulative GPA. A numerical equivalent may be requested for external use; no GPA graduation threshold is inferred.

requirements.title: Major certification
requirements.summary: The appropriate program review committee certifies the major using the completed distribution and MQP, in consultation with the student and adviser.

requirements.title: Optional double-major rules
requirements.summary: Complete both distributions and one MQP unit in each major plus one IQP unit (three project units). Appropriate shared academic work may satisfy both majors; program-review approvals apply. The more detailed Degree Options policy also permits approved interdisciplinary MQP and social-science exceptions.

requirements.title: Graduate-course use and conversion
requirements.summary: Graduate enrollment ordinarily does not require graduate admission; Business School courses require admission to a dual BS/MS program. The published conversion is one graduate credit to 1/6 undergraduate unit, processed by the Registrar.

requirements.title: Optional combined-degree approval
requirements.summary: Shared BS/MS coursework requires adviser/graduate-coordinator planning and an approved course-selection agreement submitted to the Registrar. The agreement never waives either degree’s requirements.

requirements.title: Optional BS/MS shared-credit limit
requirements.summary: Shared credit cannot exceed 40% of the master degree’s required credits; some departments limit it to 30%. The chosen graduate program and approved agreement determine the actual allowance.

requirements.title: Concentration declaration and scope
requirements.summary: A concentration requires two integrated-study units and a related MQP. Plan with the adviser and apply to the program review committee by its deadlines; concentration requirements cannot prevent completion of the major.

requirements.title: Additional-designation overlap ceiling
requirements.summary: Concentrations/minors may overlap another additional designation by at most one unit. No credit-bearing activity may be triple-counted across degree requirements or designations.

requirements.title: Double-major eligibility
requirements.summary: At most two undergraduate majors; both programs must permit the combination. Exceptions to prohibited combinations need Committee on Academic Operations approval.

requirements.title: Interdisciplinary double-major MQP alternative
requirements.summary: With advance signed approval, a 4/3-unit interdisciplinary MQP may satisfy both majors instead of two one-unit MQPs. It must cover both fields and be advised by faculty associated with both. Both program audits require certification; HUA is unchanged.

requirements.title: Social-science double-major exception
requirements.summary: A social-science MQP may also satisfy IQP when an approved one-unit project meets both sets of goals. An interdisciplinary double-major MQP cannot also be the IQP.

requirements.title: Disallowed business double majors
requirements.summary: Cannot combine this degree with Business, Financial Technology, Information Systems and Technology, Management Engineering, Marketing Analytics, except with Committee on Academic Operations approval.

requirements.title: Degree application deadline
requirements.summary: Apply to the Registrar for May graduation during the preceding A term; for September or December graduation during the preceding D term.

requirements.title: Transfer-credit approval
requirements.summary: Departments evaluate comparable accredited-institution courses individually. Normally C or better is considered; departments may require B- or higher. Vocational, correspondence, precollege/review, CEU, enrichment/refresher and CLEP work is excluded.

requirements.title: Approval before outside study
requirements.summary: After matriculation, obtain department approval and its specified minimum grade on the transfer authorization form, file before study, then submit an official transcript. Consortium work may need separate distribution approval; otherwise it may be elective credit.

requirements.title: Retroactive language credit conditions
requirements.summary: Without AP, retroactive language credit requires three high-school years averaging B, placement at least into term two, and two qualifying WPI terms graded B or better. Spanish specifically requires SP2521/2522. AP and high-school pathways cannot both earn credit.

requirements.title: Retroactive calculus credit conditions
requirements.summary: Retroactive MA1021/1022 credit follows the specified sequential WPI calculus/MA2051 pathways. Both qualifying courses must pass on first attempt by D term of year one, with no first-year NR in MA1021–1024.

requirements.title: AP and other prior-learning credit
requirements.summary: AP/IB/PLTW awards depend on the applicable examination, score and department equivalency policy. They are credit-award alternatives, not a waiver of the degree distribution. HUA AP is capped at 1/3 unit.

requirements.title: Project approval and registration
requirements.summary: An adviser must accept the project before registration. Register by the first term of work; no-penalty registration closes on term day ten. MQP supervision must include faculty associated with the major.

requirements.title: Project reporting
requirements.summary: Meet adviser expectations for interim work and a satisfactory final report. Sponsor projects normally need written/oral reports; team documentation must identify individual contributions.

requirements.title: Electronic project submission
requirements.summary: Submit the final IQP/MQP as PDF electronically with adviser approval, normally one report per team; register for at least 1/6 project unit in the submission term.

requirements.title: Degree-requirement completion recording
requirements.summary: Completion forms are due by day ten of the following term; May candidates need the eCDR by the last Thursday of D term. After day ten, recording MQP/IQP/HUA completion requires at least 1/6 unit of that activity in the current term unless a written adviser petition is approved.

requirements.title: Sponsor review and agreements
requirements.summary: Off-campus work requires proper registration and sponsor-agreement compliance. Submit sponsor copies early for confidentiality review (often 30 days); final grading/submission waits for that review.

requirements.title: Global-project overload restriction
requirements.summary: No overload during a one-term off-campus Global Projects Program project or the preceding ID2050-plus-prequalifying-project term.

requirements.title: Paid sponsored-project conditions
requirements.summary: Paid IQP/MQP work needs Undergraduate Studies approval before work: documented learning purpose, faculty control of assessment, and approved project agreement/scope. Submit by day five of the preceding term and remain registered during work; prior unregistered employment earns no project credit.

requirements.title: Fall Semester degree application
